entry.question:
## Physical scenario

A uniform bar has mass \( 0.0120\,\text{kg} \) and is \( 30.0\,\text{cm} \) long. It pivots without friction about an axis perpendicular to the bar at point \( a \). The gravitational force on the bar acts in the \( -y \)-direction. The bar is in a uniform magnetic field that is directed into the page and has magnitude \( B = 0.150\,\text{T} \).

## Question

What must be the current \( I \) in the bar for the bar to be in rotational equilibrium when it is at an angle \( 	heta = 30.0^\circ \) above the horizontal?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 4.52A

- B: B: 2.26A

- C: C: 15.1A

- D: D: 2.60A

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image shows a diagram with axes labeled \(x\) and \(y\), forming a coordinate system. There is a diagonal vector, labeled \(\vec{B}\), extending from point \(a\) on the origin to point \(b\). The vector forms an angle \(\theta\) with the x-axis. There are multiple blue crosses in the background, arranged in a grid pattern, likely representing a uniform field perpendicular to the plane of the axes. Points \(a\) and \(b\) are marked with dots.
